http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/31/alger.text: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune is seeking to reinstate the death penalty for arsonists following deadly wildfires that have ravaged parts of the country.Tebboune declared three days of national mourning on Thursday after wildfires in the northeast of the country killed at least 12 people and injured dozens more.In a statement, Tebboune described the loss of life as "a great tragedy," as officials maintained the official death toll from Wednesday.Algeria has observed a moratorium on the death penalty since 1993, but the Algerian head of state has ordered that "an amendment to the Criminal Code" be made by 15 September.12 people died, 54 in hospitalInterior Minister Saïd Sayoud confirmed five fatalities in Jijel province, four in Béjaïa, and three in Tizi Ouzou following the outbreak of the fires. He added that 54 people were receiving hospital treatment for burns, six of whom remain in critical condition.Algeria’s civil protection agency reported on Thursday morning that 46 fires remained active out of 193 recorded over the previous 24 hours. Unverified videos shared online overnight depicted sweeping blazes trapping residents in their homes.The national gendarmerie announced that three major highways linking eastern regions were closed due to forest fires raging near Béjaïa, Jijel and Sétif.While summer forest fires occur regularly in northern Algeria, more frequent droughts and extreme heat have been adding to their intensity. In July 2023, fires swept through thousands of hectares of forest and farmland near Béjaïa, destroying hundreds of homes and leaving more than 30 people dead. Authorities recorded nearly 2,000 fires nationwide in July this year alone.

Photograph: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters Belarus Trump seeks ‘massive’ Belarus fertiliser deal amid Canada trade war Trump’s announcement on Russia ally comes as he steps up his trade war with Canada, a long-term US ally and top supplier of potash Agence France-Presse Tue 22 Sep 2026 00.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google President Donald Trump has said he is working on a “massive” deal to buy fertiliser from Belarus , pivoting away from main supplier Canada amid an escalating trade dispute, and moving instead toward an ally of Russia. “The United States is working on a massive deal with respect to the purchase of Potash from Belarus,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. “The pricing would be for substantially less than we are currently paying to Canada , very good news for our farmers and ranchers.” In recent weeks Trump has stepped up his trade war with Canada , a long-term US ally and the country’s biggest supplier of potash. Whiplashed middle powers seek new alliances as Trump rages on world stage Read more The announcement on Monday shows Washington’s willingness to pursue dialogue with Minsk despite its repression of dissidents and support for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The US imports most of its potash – a chemical salt used to manufacture fertiliser – and prices soared after the Ukraine war began in 2022. In 2024, 79% came from Canada, 11% from Russia and 4% from Belarus, according to the US Geological Survey. Washington has quietly moved to thaw relations with Belarus under Trump’s second administration. Last week, Belarus freed 25 political prisoners as the US lifted sanctions on two of the country’s companies. But hundreds remain in prison after President Alexander Lukashenko, in power since 1994, suppressed mass protests over his reelection in 2020 , which was followed by a wave of sanctions. Western countries again squeezed Belarus with sanctions in 2022 after Minsk allowed Moscow to invade Ukraine through its territory. Belarus’s exiled opposition leader, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, on Monday warned that any deal with Lukashenko was “very risky”. “Our position is that it is not time to trade with the regime while all the income from potash goes to repression, goes to support of the Russian war machine,” Tsikhanouskaya told Agence France-Presse. She stressed, however, her belief that Americans “know who Lukashenko is”. https://krcgtv.com/news/local/17-year-ol.text: A 17-year-old Warsaw girl was injured in a crash Saturday evening in Benton County. According to the Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP), the crash happened around 6:33 p.m. Saturday, October 3, on US-65 south of Missouri 7. Troopers say the 17-year-old was driving a 1997 GMC Sierra southbound when she changed lanes and clipped a 2005 Chevrolet Silverado, also traveling southbound and driven by a 19-year-old Lincoln man. After the initial contact, the GMC crossed the highway, ran off the left side of the road, struck a Missouri Department of Transportation sign and overturned. The 17-year-old suffered moderate injuries and was taken by Warsaw/Lincoln EMS to Golden Valley Memorial Hospital for treatment. The report lists her safety device use as unknown. The 19-year-old driver of the Silverado was not injured. His vehicle sustained moderate damage and was towed from the scene by a family member. .The GMC was totaled and towed from the scene by Twin Lakes
